text.p: BankBoston sees huge growth potential for its operations in Brazil and Argentina and has made investment in the two countries a top corporate priority for 1997, BankBoston president and chief operating officer Henrique Meirelles said.
Meirelles told a news conference that the improved economic situation in the two South American countries after many years of near hyperinflation allowed for extraordinary business opportunities.

"We feel we have a strong competitive advantage in Latin America because of our historical presence in the region. Our priority will be to build on that presence in all countries and particularly in Brazil," he said.

Meirelles said the bank was still exploring the possibility of leveraging its growth in Brazil by acquiring a competitor after it backed out of the race to buyout Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj in December. The Banerj privatization, which has twice been postponed, is scheduled to take place in March.
"Banerj didn't work out but we're going to continue looking around. If an opportunity comes up we'll take a look. If we are interested we'll make a bid," Meirelles said.

The bank's strategy in Argentina will be to grow by seeking new depositors and opening new branches, Meirelles said. He said Argentina had recovered from a period of uncertainty following the Mexican peso crisis and that the bank was upbeat about the country's growth prospects.

Meirelles said Brazil and Argentina each represented around eight percent of BankBoston's global revenue and about the same percentage of profits. Latin America as a whole accounts for 17 percent of the bank's business.
He said recent investments in Brazil included the hiring of a new investment banking and a consumer credit team as well as the opening of several branches.
In December 1996 Banco de Boston, BankBoston's Brazil unit, had assets of $5.2 billion and total deposits of $1.5 billion.

Meirelles said BankBoston's two other corporate priorities for 1997 were the development of major corporate accounts in the United States and its retail banking business in the New England region after the acquisition of BayBanks for $2 billion in 1996.

He said the bank was currently re-evaluating its Asia strategy with an eye to developing new trade financing business among exporting Asian firms. He said the bank's new Asia policy would be announced in around 30 days.
BankBoston reported record fourth quarter earnings of $202 million. Return on average common equity was 17.7 percent.
